headline: A McKinsey Global Institute report estimates that about 11 million US workers may have to change occupations by 2035 because of AI and automation.
score_reason: Lowered 1: the report dates from September, not this week; the story is a re-report.
importance_line: It affects roughly the workers in customer service, retail, office support and warehouses, but the figure is a projection that ranges from 6 to more than 16 million depending on assumptions.
source: McKinsey Global Institute, as relayed by International Finance
summary: International Finance reports on a McKinsey Global Institute study that finds automation could cut demand for work equal to about 36 million jobs by 2035, while growth could create demand for about 41 million, so the report does not forecast mass unemployment. McKinsey describes the main challenge as helping workers move between occupations, at about 770,000 switches a year against a historical average of about 215,000.
notes: Report published in September 2026 per CBS; exact day not stated in text read.
